title: Laredo City Council to take up landlord registration, DoubleTree repairs and feral hogs
excerpt: The Laredo City Council meets Monday, November 2, at 5:30 p.m. at City Hall, with landlord registration, an update on DoubleTree repairs, and a report on feral hogs and stray animals on the agenda.
content:
The Laredo City Council is set to meet Monday, November 2, at 5:30 p.m. at City Hall, 1110 Houston Street, with a wide-ranging agenda that touches housing, downtown recovery, and animal control, according to KGNS.

Among the items up for discussion is a proposed landlord registration ordinance. According to KGNS, city leaders have said the city needs stronger tools to hold landlords accountable and keep properties maintained, and that a registration system would help with safety and compliance.

The council is also expected to receive an update on repairs to the DoubleTree by Hilton after its fire, covering repairs, code compliance, and the hotel's reopening timeline, according to KGNS.

Other agenda items include first readings for rezoning 13 properties, an ordinance to expand the city manager's authority, and a $9.98 million capital improvement bond sale, with most of the money earmarked for streets and drainage and smaller amounts for vehicles and radios, according to KGNS.

The city manager is also scheduled to report on feral hogs and stray animals, including 2,240 animal-control calls between June and October, according to KGNS.
